title: Ad-Hoc Split of Validation Responsibilities
pattern: Splitting validation responsibilities inconsistently, where some domain objects validate themselves via constructors and others rely on external validator classes.
why_bad: It breaks model self-consistency. Developers can no longer trust their intuition on whether an entity is safe to use upon instantiation, leading to unvalidated invalid states bypassing boundaries.
detection: Look for a mixture of self-validating constructors and external validation classes within the same domain model package.
counterexample: Validation frameworks designed specifically to perform multi-entity, workflow-level validations. Marked `Context-dependent`.
fix: Enforce consistent validation architecture (e.g., standardizing on smart constructors for all domain entities).
source: *Implementing Domain-Driven Design* by Vaughn Vernon (2013), p. 208-211, 286.
